To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) we can learn object detectors from weakly labeled videos and (2) training on a combination of weak and fully annotated images can improve the detector performance.

(1) we show that object detectors can be trained from videos with weak annotations, (2) we introduce an automatic method to select a representative tube from a set of videos, and (3) we show that training from videos improves the performance of detectors trained from still images.

(i) learning from videos improves the quality of the detector, (ii) learning from a combination of web videos and still images improves the quality of detectors trained from still images, and (iii) learning from videos and still images can be cast as a domain adaptation problem.
In summary, our research is concerned with
learning object detectors from weakly labeled web videos and we show how domain adaptation helps to improve performance.
learning a class specific detector from videos known only to be of the target class, i.e., without bounding-boxes.
